_note: Hidden finds (Finds). 'spot' says what tools/discovery/find_spots.tscn looked for when it chose 'pos'; FIND_PLACE=1 places any find without a pos. tests/finds_test.tscn checks every one.

finds.title: Booty Cam
finds.text: A cam, walked deep into a crack at the foot of the wall. Somebody spent a long time on it with a nut tool before they gave up. It comes out for you on the second wiggle. Climbers call this booty: stuck gear is finders keepers.
finds.rumor: Word around Camp 4: somebody bailed off the bottom of El Cap and couldn't get their cam back out. It's still in a crack near the base, off the meadow paths.

finds.title: Six-Pack Under the Needles
finds.text: In the shade behind a boulder, a pile of pine needles that's too neat. Under it, a six-pack ring with three cans of King Cobra still in it, buried to keep cool. Somebody's idea of a fridge. Somebody's loss.
finds.rumor: Somebody at Camp 4 buried a six-pack in the shade behind the boulders to keep it cool, then moved camp. In summer and fall, when the climbers are in, look off the paths.

finds.title: Chalky Stash
finds.text: Wedged under a boulder, a zip-top bag gone white with chalk. Inside: a chocolate bar, a little soft. A boulderer's emergency ration.
finds.rumor: Boulderers stash snacks under the Camp 4 boulders and forget them. Look off the path, around the rocks.

finds.title: Bail Biner
finds.text: A quickdraw hanging from a bolt low on the slabs, where somebody turned around and lowered off. You reach it from the ground on tiptoe.
finds.rumor: A party bailed off the slabs below Half Dome and left a quickdraw on a bolt. It's off the trail, along the rock.

finds.title: Forgotten Stuff Sack
finds.text: Under a fallen log, a small stuff sack. Two bags of trail mix and a chocolate bar, all sealed. Somebody's summit snacks, left at camp on the way up and forgotten on the way down. Lucky the bears didn't find it first.
finds.rumor: A backpacker lost a food sack around Little Yosemite Valley, off the trail in the trees. The bears haven't found it yet. Somebody should, before they do.

finds.title: Lost Fly
finds.text: On a gravel bar the low river has left dry, a fly hooked through a scrap of fleece: a Parachute Adams, the post still white. It must have fallen out of someone's fly patch.
finds.rumor: Greg lost a fly off his vest along the river at Leidig Meadow. When the water drops in summer and fall the gravel bars come up dry.

finds.title: Old Piton
finds.text: In a crack at the foot of the rock, an old soft-iron piton, rusted orange, its eye still bright where a carabiner rubbed it. Somebody hammered it in fifty years ago. It comes out with a tug.
finds.rumor: There's an old piton in a crack near Bridalveil, from before anybody's time. In spring the spray soaks everything; look when it's dry.

finds.title: Royal Arches Piton
finds.text: Below the Royal Arches, half buried in the leaves, a piton that fell out of a crack after seventy years of freeze and thaw. Climbers have been going up the Arches since 1936.
finds.rumor: Pitons work loose up on the Royal Arches and fall. Somebody found one in the leaves at the foot of the rock, behind The Ahwahnee.

finds.title: Railroad Spike
finds.text: In the weeds on the old rail grade, a railroad spike, square and rust-brown. The Yosemite Valley Railroad brought visitors up the Merced canyon to El Portal from 1907 until 1945; the rails are long gone, and now and then a spike turns up.
finds.rumor: The old railroad grade at El Portal still turns up a spike now and then, in the weeds off the road.

finds.title: Tin of Ski Wax
finds.text: The last of the snow has melted out from under the firs and left a dented tin of green kick wax behind, dropped by a skier touring the meadow in winter.
finds.rumor: Skiers tour around Crane Flat all winter and drop things in the snow. Come spring, when it melts out under the trees, things turn up.

finds.title: Glass Insulator
finds.text: At the foot of an old pine, half sunk in needles, a blue-green glass insulator. The telephone line it held came down long ago; the nail scar is still on the trunk above you.
finds.rumor: An old telephone line ran through the woods around Wawona. Collectors say the glass insulators still turn up under the trees.

finds.title: Light in the Brush
finds.text: A small light glowing low in the brush: a headlamp, still switched on, dropped on somebody's moonlight walk around the lake. You turn it off to save what's left of the battery.
finds.rumor: Somebody lost a headlamp walking around Mirror Lake in the dark. They say you can still see it shining at night, off the path.

finds.title: Photographer's Snack Bag
finds.text: On a rock below the wall, a little snack bag, left by someone who set up a tripod here for sunset and packed out everything but this: two handfuls of dried apricots.
finds.rumor: Photographers wait for the light at Tunnel View all afternoon and leave things on the rocks below the wall.

finds.title: Dropped Jerky
finds.text: In the shade of the firs, a resealable bag of beef jerky, still sealed. Fell out of a hip pocket on the way to Sentinel Dome, by the look of it.
finds.rumor: Hikers going up Sentinel Dome drop things in the trees off the trail.

finds.title: Lembert Booty
finds.text: A cam left in a flake at the foot of Lembert Dome, its sling sun-faded to pink. Whoever placed it lowered off and couldn't reach it again. Booty.
finds.rumor: Some climber left a cam at the bottom of Lembert Dome. Tuolumne climbers say it's still there, along the rock off the trail.

finds.title: Snowbank Cobras
finds.text: Where the last snowbank melted in the trees, two cans of King Cobra, buried to keep cold and never dug up. They're still cold.
finds.rumor: Somebody buried two cans in a snowbank up toward Dog Lake to keep them cold, and left. When the snow's gone in summer they'll show.

finds.title: Quickdraw on the Slab
finds.text: A quickdraw lying on the granite at the foot of the slabs, dropped from somewhere high. The gate still snaps shut.
finds.rumor: Somebody dropped a quickdraw off the domes above Tenaya Lake. It's down at the foot of the slabs somewhere, off the beach.

finds.title: Soggy Pack Pocket
finds.text: Caught in the roots at the river's edge, a mesh pack pocket torn off at the seam. Two bags of trail mix inside, sealed and dry.
finds.rumor: Somebody's pack pocket tore off by the river at Happy Isles. Folks say there was trail mix in it.

finds.title: Water Stop
finds.text: Behind a tree off the path, somebody's cache for the walk down the Four Mile: an empty bottle and a bag of dried apples they never came back for.
finds.rumor: Hikers coming down the Four Mile Trail leave caches in the trees at the bottom and forget them.

finds.title: Bolete Ring
finds.text: Under the firs, a ring of fat king boletes pushing up through the duff, more than you'd ever find in one place.
finds.rumor: In fall, after the first rain, the king boletes come up in rings under the firs off the Big Oak Flat Road.

finds.title: Forgotten Cooler Bag
finds.text: Behind the tent cabins, a soft cooler bag somebody set down while they packed the car and drove off without. A wedge of cheddar and two pilot bread, still good.
finds.rumor: People packing up their tent cabins at Curry Village leave things behind the rows.

finds.title: Fly in the Willows
finds.text: Snagged in a willow on the far bank, a Woolly Bugger, its marabou tail still fluffy. Somebody's back cast found the tree.
finds.rumor: Fly fishers lose flies in the willows along the Merced by Stoneman Meadow, on the far bank.

finds.title: Rim Cairn Tin
finds.text: Tucked under a flat stone back from the granite rim, a dented trail tin holding dried apricots and trail mix. Somebody packed heavy for the Pohono Trail and lightened their load.
finds.rumor: Hikers along the Pohono Trail near Taft Point tuck spare rations under stones off the granite ledges.

finds.title: South-Rim Piton
finds.text: An old forged steel piton lying in the red fir duff west of Taft Point, its eye rusted orange. Likely dropped on the walk back from a south-wall climb decades ago.
finds.rumor: Old iron climbing hardware still turns up in the red firs off the trail around Taft Point.

finds.title: Thru-Hiker's Cache
finds.text: In the shade of a whitebark pine off the John Muir Trail, a sealed sack of pilot bread and roasted whitebark pine nuts. Left behind by someone hurrying over Cathedral Pass ahead of a storm.
finds.rumor: John Muir Trail hikers sometimes drop extra rations off the path in the pines around Cathedral Lakes in summer and fall.

finds.title: Elk Hair Caddis
finds.text: Caught on a willow twig by the alpine shoreline, a neat little Elk Hair Caddis fly, still dry on a bit of tippet. Perfect for the brook trout cruising the granite drop-off.
finds.rumor: Anglers lose dry flies in the brush along the shore of Cathedral Lakes once the ice melts in summer.

finds.title: Hetch Hetchy Glass Insulator
finds.text: Half-buried in the granite grit below the canyon wall, a thick blue-green glass telegraph insulator from the 1920s dam construction line.
finds.rumor: Old blue glass insulators from the 1920s power lines still lie in the rocks off the trail at Hetch Hetchy.

finds.title: Backpacker's Dry-Bag
finds.text: Wedged beneath an oak root off the canyon trail, a rolled dry-bag holding beef jerky and dried apples. Whoever cached it on the way to Rancheria Falls forgot to grab it on the hike out.
finds.rumor: Backpackers heading out toward Rancheria Falls at Hetch Hetchy sometimes leave a food dry-bag under the oaks off the trail.

finds.title: Lost Royal Wulff
finds.text: Tangled in the alder roots along Tenaya Creek, a bright Royal Wulff dry fly with its white calf-tail wings still crisp.
finds.rumor: Somebody snagged a favorite dry fly in the brush along Tenaya Creek in spring or summer.

finds.title: Camper's Lunch Tin
finds.text: Behind a mossy log in the pines, a small snap-lid tin holding a bar of chocolate and a wedge of sharp cheddar, untouched by the jays.
finds.rumor: Campers packing out of Upper Pines sometimes leave a lunch tin back in the trees off the campground loops.

finds.title: Toll Trail Spike
finds.text: A square-cut iron spike rusted into a crack in the granite rib beside the switchbacks. McCauley and Conway's crew pinned the 1872 toll trail's cribbing to the rock with spikes like this one.
finds.rumor: Old ironwork from the 1872 toll trail still sticks out of the rock beside the Four Mile switchbacks.
